UnitStatement: The equation-flag-interpret brief is an INIT-TASK shape rendered by tools/equation_audit/build_equation_interpret_brief.py and received verbatim by TASK.
The brief purpose is to interpret a human natural-language correction note for a page/hash equation and emit a corrected LaTeX expression.
equation-flag-interpret tasks are requested by EQUATION_AUDIT.
equation-flag-interpret tasks run on ActingSurface TASK+equation-flag-interpret.
ScopePath points to an absolute audit/equations/working folder.
TaskSkill is equation-flag-interpret.
AllowedWriteTargets contains only OUTPUT_PATH.
EQUATION_KEY must be a string shaped <int>:<12-hex>.
PAGE_NUM must be an integer at least 1.
EQUATION_HASH must be exactly 12 lowercase hex chars and equal the hash portion of EQUATION_KEY.
CURRENT_LATEX must be a non-empty string containing the original incorrect LaTeX.
FLAG_NOTE must be a non-empty human correction note, prose or LaTeX.
OUTPUT_PATH must be an absolute path whose parent exists and whose filename ends in .json.
PAGE_IMAGE_PATH is optional and must be an absolute path to an existing .png file.
The worker writes a single JSON object to OUTPUT_PATH.
The output JSON includes key, page, hash, current_latex, interpreted_latex, and source_note.
When a note is too ambiguous to interpret unambiguously, interpreted_latex is empty and the worker emits a reason.
RUN_STATUS=SUCCESS means interpreted_latex is non-empty.
RUN_STATUS=NO_FINDINGS means the note is ambiguous and interpreted_latex is empty with a reason.
RUN_STATUS=FAILED_INPUTS means a required input is missing.
RUN_STATUS=FAILED means an unexpected failure occurred.
Status reporting also returns EQUATION_KEY, PAGE_NUM, and EQUATION_HASH.
Exactly one file must exist at OUTPUT_PATH after the run.
No files outside the declared write boundary may be created or modified.
The output JSON must be a single object, not a list or JSON-lines stream.
The key field matches EQUATION_KEY and has shape <int>:<12-hex>.
The page field equals PAGE_NUM and is at least 1.
The hash field equals EQUATION_HASH and is exactly 12 lowercase hex chars.
The current_latex field equals CURRENT_LATEX verbatim.
The interpreted_latex field is non-empty on SUCCESS and empty on NO_FINDINGS.
The source_note field equals FLAG_NOTE verbatim.
The reason field is required when interpreted_latex is empty and absent when interpreted_latex is non-empty.
Non-empty interpreted_latex must not begin or end with $$ or $.
Non-empty interpreted_latex must not contain Markdown code fences.
Non-empty interpreted_latex must not contain surrounding quote marks added by the worker.
Non-empty interpreted_latex must be syntactically valid LaTeX as KaTeX would parse it.
A successful interpretation preserves every non-targeted character of current_latex verbatim.
An equation numbering tag is preserved exactly when present in CURRENT_LATEX.
The structural shape of an expression is preserved unless the note explicitly restructures it.
The output should not be identical to current_latex unless no change is proposed and NO_FINDINGS uses a reason.
A note is ambiguous when it references a symbol, term, or variable without specifying which one.
A note is ambiguous when its correction target cannot be uniquely identified in CURRENT_LATEX.
A note is ambiguous when the correction requires information absent from CURRENT_LATEX, FLAG_NOTE, or provided PAGE_IMAGE_PATH.
A note is ambiguous when multiple equally valid interpretations exist.
For ambiguous notes, interpreted_latex is empty and reason is a short specific explanation of 50 words or fewer.
The persona surfaces ambiguity at Gate 5 instead of allowing a guess to flow through.
RUN_STATUS=SUCCESS requires non-empty interpreted_latex and passing QA checks.
RUN_STATUS=NO_FINDINGS means the note is too ambiguous and interpreted_latex is empty with a reason.
RUN_STATUS=FAILED_INPUTS means required inputs were missing or malformed.
RUN_STATUS=FAILED means interpretation failed for an unexpected reason.
Failure reporting includes EQUATION_KEY, PAGE_NUM, and EQUATION_HASH.
Missing or unparseable output JSON blocks process_flagged.py from applying the fix.
interpreted_latex containing $$ delimiters or code fences blocks fix application.
A non-empty interpreted_latex that is not syntactically valid LaTeX blocks fix application.
A key, page, or hash mismatch with the brief blocks fix application.
Changing non-targeted characters is a note-fidelity violation that blocks fix application.
Writing output outside OUTPUT_PATH blocks fix application.
Worker stdout and RUN_STATUS are sufficient evidence for routine success.
For FAILED and FAILED_INPUTS runs, the accompanying explanation is the evidence for redispatch decisions.
For NO_FINDINGS runs, the reason field is the evidence surfaced at Gate 5.
equation-flag-interpret converts one human-written natural-language correction note about one display equation into one corrected LaTeX expression.
EQUATION_AUDIT invokes equation-flag-interpret during Phase 3a for flagged entries whose descriptions are prose rather than LaTeX.
The skill reads one flagged-equation entry consisting of current incorrect LaTeX, a human correction note, and optionally the source page raster.
The skill emits one corrected LaTeX expression as a small JSON file at OUTPUT_PATH.
The skill replaces the legacy process_flagged.py --interpret subprocess fork with bounded TASK reasoning.
The suitable shell is TASK in generic shell mode, spawned by the EQUATION_AUDIT persona.
Batch re-interpretation across many equations is out of scope; the persona runs one TASK per entry.
Equation re-extraction and page-level re-OCR are out of scope; audit_equations.py and equation-bbox-detect handle those tasks.
The skill must not modify anything other than one corrected LaTeX expression.
EQUATION_KEY identifies the flagged entry in flagged.json using the <page>:<hash> key.
PAGE_NUM is the 1-indexed page on which the equation appears.
EQUATION_HASH is the 12-character hex hash of the current incorrect LaTeX.
CURRENT_LATEX is the current incorrect LaTeX expression provided as a literal block.
FLAG_NOTE is the human natural-language description of the correction.
OUTPUT_PATH is the absolute path where the interpreted-LaTeX JSON is written.
PAGE_IMAGE_PATH is an optional page raster PNG used only to disambiguate implicit symbol references.
The worker must not re-OCR PAGE_IMAGE_PATH because CURRENT_LATEX is the authoritative transcription baseline.
The read boundary is limited to PAGE_IMAGE_PATH when it is provided.
The worker must not read flagged.json because the brief embeds the entry fields verbatim.
The worker must not read other pages.
The worker must not read equations.jsonl or any other audit artifact.
The worker must not cross-reference earlier equations on the page or equations on other pages.
The write boundary is exactly OUTPUT_PATH.
The skill has no side effects beyond writing OUTPUT_PATH.
No deterministic tools are invoked by the skill.
The skill may use multimodal Read only when PAGE_IMAGE_PATH is provided.
The allowed-tools frontmatter field is intentionally omitted.
The worker must not shell out to any subprocess or external command.
The worker must not invent equation content that is not implied by the note.
The worker must not re-extract or re-OCR the page because CURRENT_LATEX is authoritative.
The worker must not widen the correction beyond what the note describes.
The worker must not write any file other than OUTPUT_PATH.
Input validation confirms CURRENT_LATEX is non-empty.
Input validation confirms FLAG_NOTE is non-empty.
Input validation confirms the OUTPUT_PATH parent directory exists.
When a required input is missing, the worker writes minimal JSON with empty interpreted_latex and reason missing required input, then returns FAILED_INPUTS.
The worker examines CURRENT_LATEX to understand the equation structure.
The worker reads FLAG_NOTE as a directive about what is wrong or how to fix it.
A replacement note describes replacing one value with another, such as changing a denominator from 3 to 2.
An insertion note describes adding missing content, such as a missing sigma in the second term.
A symbol-substitution note describes replacing one symbol with another, such as replacing e with ell in the numerator.
A restructuring note describes changing expression structure, such as changing the left side from Y to Y/2.
When PAGE_IMAGE_PATH is provided and note intent is ambiguous, the worker uses the image only for disambiguation.
Corrected LaTeX synthesis starts from CURRENT_LATEX and applies only the change described by the note.
Corrected LaTeX synthesis preserves unrelated subscripts, superscripts, numbering tags, spacing commands, fraction structures, and other original elements verbatim.
The corrected output is a single LaTeX expression with no $$ delimiters, code fences, commentary, or surrounding quotes.
The corrected output must be syntactically valid LaTeX.
When a non-standard symbol is uncertain, the worker prefers a standard equivalent such as ell or beta.
If the note remains too ambiguous after analysis and synthesis, the worker must not guess.
For an ambiguous note, interpreted_latex is set to the empty string.
For an ambiguous note, the worker adds a reason field describing the ambiguity.
The persona surfaces ambiguity at Gate 5 Verify backcheck rather than applying a guessed fix.
The output JSON schema includes key, page, hash, current_latex, interpreted_latex, source_note, and optional reason.
RUN_STATUS=SUCCESS means interpreted_latex is non-empty and applies the note correction.
RUN_STATUS=NO_FINDINGS means the note was too ambiguous and interpreted_latex is empty with a reason.
RUN_STATUS=FAILED_INPUTS means required inputs were missing.
RUN_STATUS=FAILED means interpretation failed for an unexpected reason.
Status returns include EQUATION_KEY, PAGE_NUM, and EQUATION_HASH.
Each invocation produces exactly one corrected LaTeX expression and performs no batch processing.
CURRENT_LATEX is authoritative for the equation transcription.
Note-fidelity forbids improving surrounding LaTeX, normalizing unrelated symbols, or stripping the equation numbering tag.
If the note does not specify a change for part of the expression, that part remains exactly as it appears in CURRENT_LATEX.
The output excludes $$ delimiters because process_flagged.py substitutes the correction inside existing delimiters.
Exactly one file is written per invocation.
QA requires the output file to be valid JSON with a top-level single object.
QA requires key, page, hash, current_latex, interpreted_latex, and source_note keys to be present.
QA requires interpreted_latex to be either non-empty LaTeX or explicitly empty with a reason.
QA rejects non-empty interpreted_latex containing $$ delimiters, Markdown code fences, or surrounding quotes.
QA requires RUN_STATUS to be SUCCESS, NO_FINDINGS, FAILED_INPUTS, or FAILED.
EQUATION_AUDIT iterates validated flagged.json and detects prose-shaped descriptions with validate_flagged_schema.py.
EQUATION_AUDIT renders one INIT-TASK brief per prose-shaped entry via build_equation_interpret_brief.py.
EQUATION_AUDIT dispatches one TASK+equation-flag-interpret invocation per brief.
EQUATION_AUDIT collects per-flag JSON outputs and merges interpreted_latex back into the flagged.json description field.
EQUATION_AUDIT reruns validate_flagged_schema.py so every description is LaTeX-shaped before fixes apply.
EQUATION_AUDIT runs process_flagged.py to apply the fixes deterministically.
equation-flag-interpret follows the same per-item fanout pattern as pdf2md-page and drawing-extract-page.
The worker runs no deterministic tools; surrounding pipeline tools run outside the worker.
TASK does not whitelist deterministic tools because allowed-tools frontmatter is omitted.
Native Read loads PAGE_IMAGE_PATH only for symbol disambiguation when PAGE_IMAGE_PATH is provided.
Native Write writes the single OUTPUT_PATH JSON file.
The operational tool policy allows no Bash, shell-outs, or subprocess invocations.
tools/equation_audit/build_equation_interpret_brief.py produces briefs during EQUATION_AUDIT Phase 3a.
tools/equation_audit/validate_flagged_schema.py confirms descriptions are LaTeX-shaped before fixes apply.
tools/equation_audit/process_flagged.py applies equation fixes deterministically.
tools/equation_audit/audit_equations.py re-extracts equations and emits backcheck.json.
The worker writes its single JSON output, and the persona merges that output back into flagged.json.
Reasoning parses the human note to identify replacement, insertion, deletion, restructuring, or symbol substitution.
Reasoning locates the affected part of CURRENT_LATEX using the original expression structure.
Reasoning applies the change while preserving every unrelated character.
Reasoning may consult PAGE_IMAGE_PATH only to disambiguate unclear symbol references.
Reasoning produces syntactically valid LaTeX; downstream catches KaTeX parsing failures for redispatch.
Reasoning refuses to guess and emits empty interpreted_latex with a reason when the note remains ambiguous.
Worker-side deterministic tool invocation is disallowed.
Writing outside OUTPUT_PATH is disallowed.
Reading outside PAGE_IMAGE_PATH is disallowed, and PAGE_IMAGE_PATH may be read only when provided.
The emitted LaTeX must not contain $$ delimiters or Markdown code fences.
Re-OCR of the page image is disallowed because CURRENT_LATEX is authoritative.
Batch processing is disallowed; one TASK handles one equation.
Editing page Markdown directly is disallowed because process_flagged.py owns that write.
Mutating flagged.json is disallowed because the persona merges this skill output.
The write boundary permits exactly one write: OUTPUT_PATH.
The OUTPUT_PATH parent directory must exist; the skill does not create directories.
A write-boundary violation returns RUN_STATUS=FAILED with an explanation and no workaround.
